The conflict: applicant register says "Mettler-Toledo Inc." and document says "Mettler-Toledo, LLC".

Both refer to Mettler-Toledo, the weighing instrument company. The difference is "Inc." vs "LLC" — legal-suffix drift. The rules say legal-suffix drift = same-entity. So verdict: same-entity.

Now best_value: for same-entity, what's the best value? The rules say for different-entity, best_value = document's. For same-entity with number/year format, register canonical form. For general same-entity (spelling drift, legal-suffix drift), which value should the fused record carry? The certificate document is the legal instrument, so arguably document value. But the rules only explicitly say register canonical form for number/year format differences. Hmm.

The general principle stated: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)." This implies that when same-entity, the fused record could take either; but consistency suggests... The register is the canonical database. For same-entity cases the rule only specifies register's canonical form for number/year format differences. For spelling/suffix drift, it's ambiguous. But given the document is the legal instrument, and the document says "Mettler-Toledo, LLC", one might pick the document. However, a conservative fusion approach often prefers the register as the curated canonical source, with document only overriding for different-entity.

Given the rules: same-entity — no explicit best_value directive except number/year case (register canonical). The safest reading: for same-entity, keep register canonical form (since document only overrides when it's genuinely a different entity, in which case register was wrong). So best_value = "Mettler-Toledo Inc." from register.

I'll answer: verdict same-entity, best_value "Mettler-Toledo Inc.", why: Inc./LLC is legal-suffix drift referring to the same Mettler-Toledo corporate family, so register's canonical form is kept.
